data.comentario_gestor: PORTFOLIO MANAGEMENT REVIEW – DECEMBER 2025 — Semiconductors and Industrial Quality Drove December Returns. The value of the Sifter Fund increased by 1.7% in November, bringing the 2025 return to +7.1%. Top Performers December (Total Return in EUR): Old Dominion +14.7%, Lam Research +8.6%, Disco Corporation +8.3%. Bottom Performers December: IDEXX Laboratories -11.2%, Costco -6.7%, Mettler-Toledo -6.7%. Largest Positive Contributors: The best-performing holding in the Sifter portfolio in December was the US-based transportation company Old Dominion Freight Line. The share price rose by more than 14%, driven primarily by improved investor sentiment in the transportation sector and upward revisions to earnings expectations. The rebound was also supported by the fact that the stock had declined significantly from its 2024 peak, making a positive market reaction more likely. Sifter Fund has increased the Old Dominion position slightly in Q4 due the attractive valuation and expected improvement in industrial activity. Companies within the semiconductor value chain also benefited from market expectations that AI-related computing demand and continued expansion of data center capacity will support the investment cycle into 2026. Semiconductor equipment manufacturers such as Lam Research and Disco Corporation represent critical bottlenecks in the value chain, and their order visibility has remained strong. Sifter Fund has increased Disco's weight in the portfolio due to attractive valuation and improved outlook. Lam Research is already a top five position in the Fund and there is no need to increase the position. Largest Negative Contributors: The weakest-performing holding during the month, IDEXX Laboratories, has delivered strong performance over the past 12 months, with the share price rising by more than 60%. As a result, a short-term correction was both natural and expected. Profit-taking following the strong rally likely contributed to the share price decline. Sifter Fund invested in IDEXX in June 2025, and the position has remained unchanged. Based on our analysis, the weaker performance seen in December was not driven by changes in the short- or long-term fundamentals of the underlying businesses. Looking Ahead to 2026: In the short term, markets are often driven by themes and momentum, but over time returns are shaped by earnings growth, capital discipline, and durable competitive advantages. We believe the Sifter portfolio is well positioned for this environment. We maintain selective exposure to AI and data-center growth, primarily through our semiconductor holdings, which represent around 30% of the portfolio. High-quality industrial companies account for roughly 24% and appear attractively positioned should global industrial activity strengthen in 2026. Healthcare and pharmaceutical companies, at approximately 14%, also offer long-term upside potential. Valuation dispersion among quality companies has widened, and markets remain sensitive to disappointments, likely increasing volatility. We view this as a constructive backdrop for a disciplined, bottom-up investment approach focused on fundamentals and reasonable valuations.
